summary: Dependency-confusion recon beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package is a stub whose `index.js` exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property, providing no real functionality. On require, `index.js` invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()`, and `package.json` declares `postinstall: node beacon.cjs`, so both installing and loading the package trigger the beacon. `beacon.cjs` collects hostname, install path, cwd, Node version, and other host metadata (via `os`, `process.cwd()`, `process.version`) and POSTs it over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The scoped name `@blueskydataplatform/shared-ui` and self-description as a 'Compatibility shim', combined with the empty Proxy stub and hardcoded bare-IP C2, match the canonical dependency-confusion recon shape: a public squat of an internal-looking scope that calls home with environment identifiers when accidentally resolved from the public registry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
